scHiCARdownstream Vignette: scHiCAR downstream analysis via ArchR

Jianhong Ou

20 May 2026

Source: vignettes/scHiCARdownstream.Rmd
scHiCARdownstream.Rmd

Abstract

scHiCARdownstream is a R package for scHiCAR downstream analysis via ArchR.

Introduction

Installation 

if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("jianhong/scHiCARdownstream")

Quick start

There are five main steps to use scHiCARdownstream for downstream analysis of scHiCAR data:

Step 1. Load the required library.

library(scHiCARdownstream)
library(ArchR)
library(BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10)

Step 2. Read RNA-DNA barcode map.

barcodeMap <- read.csv(system.file('extdata', 'barcode.map.csv', package='scHiCARdownstream'))
bmap <- barcodeMap$`DNA`
names(bmap) <- barcodeMap$`RNA`

Step 3. Create ArchR project

extdata <- system.file('extdata', package = 'scHiCARdownstream')
rnaFiles <- dir(file.path(extdata, 'RNA'), 'matrix.mtx.gz',
                full.names=TRUE, recursive=TRUE)
atacFiles <- dir(file.path(extdata, 'ATAC'), 'ATAC.tsv.gz$',
                 full.names = TRUE)
names(rnaFiles) <- names(atacFiles) <- 'dpa7'
addArchRGenome("mm10")
proj <- createArchRproj(
    rnaFiles, atacFiles,
    bmap, barcodesFun=function(x){
      do.call(rbind, strsplit(colnames(x), '_'))[, 4]
    },
    outputDirectory = "ArchR_proj",
    annotationGenes = NULL,
    verbose=TRUE
    )

Step 4. Process the data

proj <- processArchR(proj, skip_rmDup=TRUE) ## data are not good for rm doublets.
## Modularity Optimizer version 1.3.0 by Ludo Waltman and Nees Jan van Eck

## Maximum modularity in 10 random starts: 0.6168
## Number of communities: 2
## Elapsed time: 0 seconds
## Modularity Optimizer version 1.3.0 by Ludo Waltman and Nees Jan van Eck
##

## Number of edges: 7235
## 
## Running Louvain algorithm...
## Maximum modularity in 10 random starts: 0.6078
## Number of communities: 2
## Elapsed time: 0 seconds
plotEmbedding(proj, 
              name = "Clusters_Combined",
              embedding = "UMAP_Combined",
              size = 1, labelAsFactors=F, labelMeans=F)

# and call peaks, make sure macs2 available or provide the path via parameter `pathToMacs2`.
proj <- callPeaks(proj)

Step 5. prepare files for FastHigashi

pairs_files <- dir(file.path(extdata, 'Pairs'), 'pairs.gz', full.names = TRUE)
names(pairs_files) <- 'dpa7'
prepareHigashiFiles(proj, pairs_files)

Step 6. run FastHigashi (ask Higashi installed)

This step as Higashi and FastHigashi installed. The parameter use_conda is still in test.

runFastHigashi()

Step 7. prepare files for scDeepLUCIA

Generate the bigwig files for ATAC reads for each sample

ArchR::getGroupBW(proj, groupBy = "Sample",
                  normMethod = "nFrags",
                  tileSize = 25, # tileSize 25 is required by scDeepLUCIA
                  maxCells = 1000)
## [1] "/__w/scHiCARdownstream/scHiCARdownstream/vignettes/ArchR_proj/GroupBigWigs/Sample/dpa7-TileSize-25-normMethod-nFrags-ArchR.bw"

Run scripts to create the Epi array files. Note the script ask pyBigWig and numpy installed.

# Retrieve path to the script within your package
script_path <- system.file("extdata", "scripts", "prepare_scDeepLUCIA_epi.py",
                           package = "scHiCARdownstream")
# rewrite the sys.argv for argparse.ArgumentParser
sys <- reticulate::import("sys")
sys$argv <- list(
    script_path,
    "--bw_roots", file.path(ArchR::getOutputDirectory(proj), 'GroupBigWigs', 'Sample'),
    "--marker_name", 'r2_030M',
    "--resolution", 5000,
    "--outdir", "scDeepLUCIA_inputs/sliced_epi_array/mm10",
    "--nan_to", 0.0
  )
# Run the Python script
reticulate::py_run_file(script_path)

Create one-hot encoded genomic feature npy file.

createOnehotGenomicNpy(proj, resolution=5000)

Create 5kb-resolution contact matrix npy file.

createContactMatrix(proj, pairs_files)
